problem: Persistent open-vocabulary multi-object navigation systems like OneMap rely on foundation-model inference, dense feature projection, map movement, frontier processing and repeated detection, which are too slow and memory/energy hungry for power-constrained edge GPUs.
motivation: Robots need to search for sequential language-specified objects while reusing semantic evidence, but on-board deployment on devices like Jetson AGX Orin is limited by compute, RAM and power. The paper observes the workload is dominated by several coupled bottlenecks that can be reorganized jointly rather than optimized in isolation.
key_idea: Reorganize the OneMap pipeline into a hardware-aware dataflow (compiled mixed-precision perception, direct-to-map confidence-weighted feature aggregation, accelerator-resident maps, compiled navigation ops) with detector scheduling driven by current-view target similarity.
insight: Removing the dense image-resolution feature intermediate and running the semantic map and navigation ops on-accelerator, together with scheduling target-confirmation detection only when current-view target similarity warrants it, gives large speedups with small accuracy loss. Per the abstract, the coordinated dataflow and current-view target-conditioned execution are the effective mechanisms. Only the abstract was available, so no per-component ablation details are known.
method: Compiled mixed-precision perception: foundation-model inference compiled and run in mixed precision on the edge GPU.
Direct-to-map confidence-weighted feature aggregation: projects features straight into the semantic map, eliminating the dense image-resolution feature intermediate.
Accelerator-resident semantic maps: the persistent map is kept on the GPU to avoid data movement.
Compiled navigation operations: frontier processing and other navigation ops are compiled for the accelerator.
Language-conditioned detector scheduling: triggers target-confirmation detection based on current-view target similarity to avoid repeated detection.

setting.backbone: OneMap-style pipeline with frozen foundation models (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; reuses OneMap's pretrained foundation models)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (assumed from OneMap; not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: frontier-based exploration / map-based planning (not stated in abstract)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) plus hardware-in-the-loop on Jetson AGX Orin

numbers_note: abstract only; relative results given (92.6% and 96.1% retention of reproduced OneMap single- and multi-object SR) but no absolute metric values
results: On complete HM3D benchmarks, the implementation retains 92.6% and 96.1% of the reproduced OneMap single- and multi-object success rates. Across 36 paired hardware-in-the-loop comparisons on a Jetson AGX Orin at four power modes, it achieves geometric-mean speedups of 4.64x on-device computation and 3.55x complete episode duration, with 51.21% lower peak RAM and 75.32% lower energy proxy, preserving every paired outcome.
limitations: Success rate is reduced to 92.6% (single-object) of the reproduced OneMap.
Evaluated against a single reference system (OneMap) on one edge platform (Jetson AGX Orin); no real-robot deployment stated.
Energy is measured with a summed board-rail proxy rather than a true system energy measurement.
